rationale: Anchors the hallucination–illusion distinction immediately after the perceptual disturbances content block; a classic exam trap corrected by recall.
Tests application of the lucid-interval concept and ICD-11 documentation requirements in a forensic context after the forensic-implications content block.
Tests precise knowledge of McNaughten's Rules and BNS Section 22 immediately after the content block — targets the 'two prongs only, no irresistible impulse' accuracy point.
Tests the Ganser syndrome distinction after its dedicated content block — a high-yield trap where students confuse a genuine dissociative disorder with malingering.
Anchors the 48–72 hour alcohol-withdrawal timeline immediately after the pathophysiology content block — the most commonly mis-stated fact in DT questions.
Tests the thiamine-before-glucose rule and Wernicke encephalopathy prevention in a clinical management scenario after the assessment and management content block.
Tests knowledge of MHA 2017 admission types after the admission-procedures content block — focuses on the voluntary/supported/magistrate-ordered framework and the Act's identity (NOT 1987).
Tests Section 115 decriminalisation of attempt to suicide — a landmark provision that forensic physicians must cite accurately.
